title: skills(formula): teach that a date / datetime field is text in CEL, so a Timestamp-only call needs date(…) first (isoDate(date(record.start_at)))
body:
domain:server#4 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgWRcTEB3toGxnWvuvX

Skills-docs follow-up of #32595 (PR #32817, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`). That PR makes the authoring gate refuse a `date` or `datetime` field handed straight to a call that takes only a Timestamp (`isoDate(record.start_at)`, `record.start_date.getFullYear()`), with the new refusal `date-text-call` and the rewrite `isoDate(date(record.start_at))`. At runtime such a field is its ISO text, so those calls faulted on every record.

`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` line 163 (the Dates table's `isoDate(t)` / `isoDatetime(t)` row) says "Text in? `isoDate(date(s))`" but never says that a date or datetime field IS text, so an agent writes `isoDate(record.start_at)` and now meets a refusal.

## Do

- In the Dates section, one line: a `date` / `datetime` field reads as its ISO text; wrap it in `date(…)` before a Timestamp-only call or method (`isoDate(date(record.start_at))`, `date(record.start_date).getFullYear()`); concatenating it with text and ordering it against a text literal work on the text as is.
- Name the refusal word `date-text-call` where the skill lists refusals, if it does.
- Add or extend one eval prompt that formats a datetime field's day and expects `isoDate(date(record.<field>))`.

Blocked-by: #32817
